newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo in Zantac generic deal with NovoPharm.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo in Zantac generic deal with NovoPharm.

text.p: British drugs company Glaxo Wellcome Plc said on Thursday it had signed a licensing agreement to allow its rival NovoPharm Inc. to market a generic form of Glaxo's ulcer treatment Zantac.

Under the terms of the deal, NovoPharm will be able to market its generic treatment 16 days earlier than other manufacturers, a Glaxo spokesman said. In return, Glaxo will receive unspecified payments from NovoPharm.
Glaxo, the world's biggest drugs company, said it was also dropping plans to appeal against a recent court ruling which allowed NovoPharm to market its generic alternative to Zantac from mid-July.
Glaxo shares dropped as low as 1,150 pence on the news before climbing back to 1,156 in early afternoon trade, down 9-1/2 pence on the day.
The company had warned in March it faced two lean years after its patent on Zantac -- its best-selling drug and the foundations of its international fortune -- expires in July.
Its chief executive designate Sean Lance said on Wednesday that the company was braced for the loss of the money-spinning treatment.
Glaxo has been pushing its new products, such as HIV and AIDS treatments Retrovir and Epivir, and has said it is confident it can kick-start growth from 1999.
Earlier this month the firm posted promising trial results on a new drug for treating Hepatitis B which raised market hopes Glaxo may have discovered a new blockbuster.
